meta.title: Hugo Menz · Working systems
meta.description: Five inspectable automation, application and workflow case studies.

hero.title: Systems you can open, test and inspect.
hero.lead: Five real cases across automation, applications and workflows. No invented results, with the technical state kept visible.

approach.title: The boundaries are part of the work.
approach.copy: Every case says what is built, what uses synthetic data and what remains architecture. Public demos need no credentials and contain no real data.
approach.one: An interface that demonstrates the flow

rfq.name: Menz RFQ Copilot
rfq.summary: A fit check for complex technical requests before an offer is prepared.
rfq.problem: Sales and engineering receive requirements spread across forms, email and documents. Contradictions can surface late.
rfq.solution: Structures the request, separates evidence from questions, flags contradictions and prepares customer questions.
rfq.how: Load the sample, run the analysis and inspect the decision, blockers, evidence and reply draft.
rfq.working: Interface, multimodal analysis, deterministic rules, evidence and review agents, and provider rate-limit fallback.
rfq.simulated: The demo uses a synthetic RFQ and does not represent a real customer.
rfq.experimental: Company-specific rules and knowledge need configuration before production use.
rfq.tech: React, TypeScript, Vite, n8n, PDF and image analysis.
rfq.imageAlt: Menz RFQ Copilot analysing a synthetic technical request

rag.name: Second Brain RAG Security Lab
rag.summary: A visual lab showing how a malicious note can influence a RAG workflow.
rag.problem: Retrieved content can contain instructions, and a valid citation does not prove an answer is grounded.
rag.solution: Reproduces attacks with synthetic notes, exposes the chain of custody and compares original and hardened behavior.
rag.how: Choose an attack, edit the note and follow retrieval, context, quarantine and answer validation.
rag.working: Contracts, Supabase functions, n8n workflows, security tests and two reproduced mitigations.
rag.simulated: The demo is deterministic in the browser and calls neither a model nor a private database.
rag.experimental: Owner identity through a trusted header remains a conditional risk pending signing and expiry.
rag.tech: Next.js, Supabase, n8n, OpenRouter, Python and contract tests.
rag.imageAlt: RAG security lab comparing exposed and hardened retrieval workflows

fridge.name: FridgeFlow
fridge.summary: A mobile view for deciding what food to use first without treating estimates as safety advice.
fridge.problem: A household inventory loses value when dates, prepared meals and uncertainty are mixed together.
fridge.solution: Prioritises use today, use soon, prepared and needs confirmation, with manual or Telegram input.
fridge.how: Explore the synthetic household, open items and inspect activity and connections. Mutations are disabled in the demo.
fridge.working: Responsive application, Supabase model, actions, events and a prepared Telegram integration.
fridge.simulated: The public Pages build uses a synthetic household and requires no login.
fridge.experimental: Voice interpretation and automation need configured services and credentials.
fridge.tech: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Supabase and n8n.
fridge.imageAlt: FridgeFlow showing food priorities with synthetic household data

agent.name: Agent Observatory
agent.summary: An observatory for executions, conversations, commits, events and an external kill switch.
agent.problem: An agent system is difficult to evaluate when decisions and changes are not visible.
agent.solution: Brings conversation, evidence, commits and operating limits into one surface.
agent.how: Select a synthetic run, read each agent, inspect the commit, the blocked event and the control boundary.
agent.working: Two Angular applications, nine validated workflows, Supabase model and a public trace dashboard.
agent.simulated: Pages uses a synthetic trace and disables controls that require administrator access.
agent.experimental: The workflows have not yet been verified together in a production n8n runtime.
agent.tech: Angular, TypeScript, Supabase, n8n and GitHub Actions.
agent.imageAlt: Agent Observatory showing a synthetic multi-agent trace

music.name: Music School Automation
music.summary: A simple course and schedule enquiry with a structured Telegram handoff.
music.problem: A person wants to ask about lessons without understanding the internal timetable or completing a long form.
music.solution: Guides course, level, day and contact, then prepares one concise message for a human reply.
music.how: Choose a synthetic course, complete the enquiry and inspect the exact Telegram notification preview.
music.working: Responsive application, payload validation and an inactive, importable n8n workflow.
music.simulated: The demo sends no data and only prepares a browser preview.
music.experimental: A future conversational assistant is described as architecture, not implemented.
music.tech: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, n8n and Telegram.
music.imageAlt: Music School application with synthetic courses and enquiry form
